transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I guess I'm here because... well, work has been a little tricky lately. I'm a construction manager, and, you know, I try really hard to do a good job. But I've been having this thing where I'll start a safety briefing or, like, sit down for a plan review, and I really, really try to pay attention. But then, within a few minutes, my mind is just... off thinking about three other problems on the job site. And then I end up missing things that I know I should have caught. It's not because I don't care, I promise. I just... I don't know, is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Are you noticing any difficulties with focus or getting things done outside of your job as well?

Um, well... yeah, a little bit, I guess. I mean, my wife is a saint, she really is. But I think I’m... well, I’m probably wearing her down lately. I'll tell her I’m going to handle something at the house, and I fully intend to, but it just completely slips my mind. She ends up having to remind me over and over about things I already promised I'd do. I feel terrible about it, honestly, because I really try to be a good husband. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? 

And, um... I should probably be completely honest with you. I didn't want you to think I was just making excuses earlier, but the work thing is actually a bit worse than I made it sound. It’s gotten bad enough that... well, because of some missed follow-ups and my site coordination getting a little disorganized, my employer actually sat me down and gave me a formal notice of concern. I'm trying so, so hard to fix it, I promise. I really want to get back on track. Does that all make sense?
How is your relationship with your wife being affected by these issues with forgetfulness and disorganization?

Um... well, it's... I mean, she's amazing, like I said. We're good, mostly. It's just... I guess she gets a little frustrated sometimes? Which is completely fair, I know it is. I'll forget to, you know, fix the leaky faucet or pay a bill I said I'd handle, and she has to pick up the slack. 

She hasn't... I mean, we're not fighting all the time or anything like that. I don't want you to think we have a bad marriage. I just... I hate letting her down, you know? I really want to be the guy she can rely on. I'm trying to be better about writing things down so she doesn't have to nag—well, not nag, just remind me. I really am trying to be a good partner. Does that sound like a normal thing couples go through, or... is that what you were looking for?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Um, restless? No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I'm a pretty energetic guy, you know? Being in construction, I'm used to being on my feet and moving around a lot. So, sitting still for a long time can be a little... well, I guess anyone would get a little stiff or want to stretch their legs after a while, right? 

I don't think I'm fidgety in a bad way. I might tap my foot a little or shift in my chair if a meeting is running really long, but I always try to be respectful and pay attention. I certainly don't want to be a distraction to anyone else. I really do try to sit quietly when I need to. Is that... I mean, does that sound okay? Or were you meaning something more extreme than that?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Um... interrupt? I mean, I really try not to. I know how rude that can be, and I always want to be respectful of people's time and conversations. I'm definitely not trying to be that guy who just talks over everybody. 

But, um... I guess maybe sometimes on the job site, I can get a little ahead of myself? Like, if I see two subcontractors talking, or if someone is, you know, working through some paperwork, I might... well, I might just walk up and jump right in with my own point before they've actually asked for my input or finished what they were saying. It's just because I want to keep things moving and make sure the job gets done right, you know? I'm just eager to help. But I think maybe it rubs some people the wrong way sometimes. I really don't mean anything bad by it, I promise. I just get so focused on getting the project done. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a jerk to work with.
Do you often blurting out answers before questions have been completed?

Oh, um... well, I definitely try to be a good listener. I really do. But... I guess sometimes, maybe, I get a little over-eager? 

Like, someone on the crew will start asking me something about a materials order or a timeline, and... well, my brain just kind of jumps ahead. I'll think I already know exactly where their question is going, so I just... I kind of cut them off and answer. I'm really just trying to save them time and be efficient, you know? But then... yeah, sometimes I answer a little too fast, and I'll realize I completely missed the most important part of what they hadn't actually said yet. 

And then I feel terrible about it. I really hate making mistakes like that, especially when I'm just trying to be helpful and keep the project moving. I don't want anyone to think I don't care about what they have to say. Is that... do a lot of people do that? I'm really trying hard to get better at just waiting until the end of the sentence, I promise.
Have you noticed any changes in your friendships or social relationships outside of work due to these issues?

Um... outside of work? Well, I mean, my friends are pretty understanding guys, mostly. We're all busy, so if I forget to text back or show up a little late to watch the game, they don't usually make a huge deal out of it. I try really hard to be a good friend, I do. 

But... I guess things at home have been a little tense lately. My wife, she's wonderful, she really is. But she's just... I think she's getting kind of worn down. I'll promise to handle something around the house, like fixing the sink or paying a bill, and I really mean to do it! But then I get distracted, and she has to keep reminding me. I hate making her feel like she has to manage me. I want to be a good husband, you know? I feel awful that it puts so much on her. 

And, um... since you asked about how things are going overall, I probably should mention... work has actually been a little rougher than I let on earlier. I always try to do my best, but lately, some of the site coordination has been a bit disorganized, and I've missed a few follow-ups. It actually got to the point where my boss brought it up as a formal concern. I was so embarrassed. I really pride myself on being a hard worker. I'm trying so hard to get a better system in place so I don't let anyone down again. Does that... I mean, is it normal to struggle this much with keeping everything straight? I just want to fix it so I'm doing a good job for everyone.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or stressed by the impact of these issues on your daily life and relationships?

Um... overwhelmed? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm, like, falling apart or anything. I'm a pretty positive guy, you know? I always try to keep a good attitude and just push through things. I really believe if you work hard enough, you can figure anything out. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... yeah, maybe a little stressed? Just because I care so much about doing a good job for my boss and being a good partner to my wife. When I feel like I'm letting them down, even when I'm trying my absolute hardest, it just... it feels pretty heavy sometimes. I just want everyone to be happy with me, and it's frustrating when my brain just won't cooperate with what I want to do. 

I'm managing, though! I really am. I don't want you to think I'm not handling my life. I just... I really want to find a way to make things run smoother so I don't have to worry so much about dropping the ball. Is it okay that I feel a little stressed about all this? I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything. I'm really ready to do whatever it takes to get better.
Are these issues affecting your ability to complete tasks or achieve your goals on a daily basis?

Well, I mean, I definitely get a lot done every day. I'm always moving, always trying to keep the site running smooth. But... um... I guess sometimes finishing every single step of a task can be... a little tricky for me? 

Like, say we do a site walk, and someone gives me a list of things to follow up on. I always jump right on it! I'll handle the first one or two things right away, because I really want to be on top of it and show I'm proactive. But then... you know how construction is, there's always a fire to put out. I'll get pulled into something else, and... well, I'll find out way later that I never actually sent the email, or I didn't call the subcontractor to fully close out the issue. 

I feel so bad when that happens, because I don't want anyone thinking I'm lazy or leaving things half-done. I really do intend to finish it all! It's just hard when there are so many moving parts. I'm trying to write things down more so I don't miss those last steps. Does that sound like a normal thing to struggle with when you're busy? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to fix it, because I really want to be reliable for my team.
Are you feeling like these issues are impacting your overall well-being or ability to function in your daily life?

Um... well... I guess I'd say I'm still functioning okay, mostly. I get up, I go to work, I try to keep a smile on my face. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around unable to do anything, because I really do try my best every single day. 

But... yeah, I suppose it is impacting things more than I'd like to admit. Like I mentioned earlier, the work stuff... it's gotten bad enough that my boss actually made it a formal concern. Just with the missed follow-ups and the site coordination getting a little messy. I really hated that happening, because I want to be someone they can count on. 

And then at home... it's just hard seeing my wife so worn down. I tell her I'll handle things, and I mean it, I really do! But then I forget, and she has to remind me, and... it just makes me feel like I'm making her life harder instead of being a good partner. 

So... I guess, yes, it is affecting my daily life. I just want to get it sorted out so I can be the guy everyone needs me to be. Is it normal to feel this bad about letting people down? I just really want to fix it.
Are you having trouble maintaining any of your friendships due to your current issues?

Um... friendships? No, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble with that. I'm a pretty social guy, you know? I get along with pretty much everyone on the site, and I've got a good group of buddies I've known for a long time. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I might be a little late to a barbecue, or I might forget to text someone back right away if things get crazy at work, but they know me! They know I don't mean anything by it. We always have a good time when we do catch up. 

I try really hard to be a good friend and show up when it counts. I don't think any of my friends are upset with me or anything like that. Do you think it's okay that I'm not struggling in that area? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
Are you worried that your wife might leave you due to your forgetfulness and disorganization?

Oh, um... leave me? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, we love each other very much! 

I know I said she gets worn down, and... well, yeah, she does get frustrated when I forget things or when the house gets a little chaotic. But she knows my heart's in the right place, you know? She knows I'm not doing it on purpose. We always talk it out, and I always promise to try harder, which I really, really do. 

I don't want to make it sound like our marriage is falling apart or anything, because it's not. She's incredibly supportive. I just... I just hate feeling like a burden sometimes. But she hasn't said anything about leaving. That's... that's not something I should be worried about, right? I mean, couples go through rough patches with this kind of stuff all the time, don't they? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to be a good husband so it never even gets to that point.
Do you feel like your current issues are preventing you from doing the things you want or need to do on a daily basis?

Um... well, preventing me from doing things? I wouldn't say *preventing*, exactly. I mean, I still get things done! I really try to push through and make sure I'm taking care of my responsibilities. 

I guess... sometimes things take me a little longer than they should, or I might have to circle back to something I started earlier. Like, I might have grand plans for the weekend to fix the deck and clean out the garage, and maybe I only get halfway through one of those things. But I'm still out there working hard, you know? I don't just give up. 

I don't want you to think I'm completely incapable or anything. I just... maybe I don't always finish everything on my to-do list exactly when I want to. But I always get there eventually! Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right. I just want to make sure you know I'm really trying my best to stay on top of it all.
Are you feeling like these issues are significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy your daily activities or maintain healthy relationships?

Um... significantly interfering? I mean, I really try not to let it get to that point. I still enjoy things! I really do. I love my job, and I love my family. 

I guess... well, I wouldn't say it's ruining my life or anything, but... maybe it's causing a few more hiccups than I'd like to admit. Like at work... I try so hard to keep everything running smoothly, but recently... well, there were some missed follow-ups, and the site coordination got a little messy. My boss actually brought it up, like, a formal concern. Which was awful, because I always want to do a good job for them. I promised I'd get a better system in place. 

And at home... I know I mentioned my wife gets frustrated. It's just... she's so patient, but I know she's getting worn down from having to remind me about things I swore I was going to handle. I hate putting that on her. 

But I'm here, right? I'm trying to fix it. I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything fall apart. I'm really working on it. Does that sound like what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can get this sorted out.
Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder or taken any medication for it?

Oh, um... no, no, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with anything like that, and I've definitely never taken any medication for it. 

I mean, I've always just thought I was a little scatterbrained, you know? Just... maybe a bit more energetic or disorganized than the next guy. I never really thought it was something medical that needed a diagnosis or pills or anything. I always figured if I just worked a little harder or made a better list, I could get it under control on my own. 

I really hope I haven't been doing something wrong by not getting checked out sooner. I just... I didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing, you know? Do you think I should have looked into this earlier? I just always tried my best to handle it myself.
Have you experienced these issues with focus, organization, and follow-through your entire life, or did they start at some point?

Um... my whole life? Well, I guess... yeah, it's kind of always been there. But I don't want it to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I was just... really enthusiastic, I guess. 

I mean, if I think way back to elementary school, I know my teachers would talk to my parents sometimes. They'd say things like I couldn't stay in my seat, or I'd talk out of turn... just eager to participate, you know? And, well, maybe I lost my homework a few times, or I'd rush through the directions before I really understood what they wanted me to do. But I always meant well! I was just so ready to jump right in. 

I really tried to be a good student, I promise. It's just always been a little harder for me to slow down and keep everything straight. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of background you were looking for. I just don't want you to think I was a troublemaker or anything.
Do you often feel the need to be constantly active or have trouble engaging in quiet leisure activities?

Um... constantly active? No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely like to stay productive! With my job on the construction sites, I'm always on my feet, which is great because I really enjoy working hard and being useful. But I wouldn't say I *have* to be active all the time. 

And quiet activities... I think I do okay with those? I mean, I might not be the kind of guy who sits down and reads a massive book for hours, but I can definitely relax. Like, when my wife wants to put on a movie, I sit there with her. I mean, maybe I'll get up a couple of times to grab a water or check if I locked the front door, but I'm still spending that quiet time with her. I really try to be present for that, I promise. 

I definitely don't feel like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. I can definitely unwind when I'm supposed to... is that what you were asking about?
Do you often feel like you're fidgeting or unable to stay still when you're in a quiet environment?

Um... fidgeting? No, I don't think I do that. I mean, I try really hard to be respectful when it's supposed to be quiet, you know? Like if I'm in a meeting with the contractors or something, I know how to sit and listen. 

I guess I might shift in my chair a bit, or maybe tap my pen sometimes, but... that's just normal, right? Just keeping the blood flowing. I'm definitely not, like, squirming around or bothering anybody. I always want to make sure I'm being polite and paying attention. I hope that makes sense? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm disruptive or can't handle myself in a professional setting.
Did you experience difficulties with focus, organization, and follow-through as a child?

Um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit? When you asked about my whole life? 

But, um, just to be sure I'm answering right... yeah, I guess I did have some of those things going on when I was a kid. Like I said before, I was just really eager and maybe a little rushed sometimes. I always wanted to do a good job on my schoolwork, I really did! It just... sometimes the organization part didn't come as naturally to me. 

But I wasn't a bad kid, I promise. I always tried my best to be helpful and participate. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need without repeating myself too much. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Do you experience difficulties with focus and organization at home and at work, or is it mostly in one of those environments?

Um... I guess it's a little bit of both? But I really try my best in both places, I promise! 

At work... well, there have been a couple of hiccups recently. Just minor things, really! Like, maybe a few missed follow-ups or some coordination stuff on the sites that got a little jumbled. My boss did, um, sit down with me to express some concern about it. But I'm working really hard to get a better system in place so I don't let anyone down again. I just want to be a good manager for my team, you know?

And at home... well, my wife is a saint, she really is. But I think she gets a little worn out sometimes. I'll tell her I'm going to handle something around the house, and I completely mean to do it right then, but... somehow it slips my mind, and she has to remind me. I feel terrible about it because I want to be a good husband and take care of things for her. 

I really am trying to do better in both places. I hope that doesn't make me sound too irresponsible? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, like you asked. Is that the kind of information you needed?
